subject.title: feat(exec): verified-human instruction provenance for sensitive targets

question: Should OpenClaw add a core or gateway-enforced verified-human instruction provenance contract for sensitive side-effect targets, and which public config/plugin/API shape should own it?
rationale: The remaining work changes security-boundary semantics, operator policy, config, approvals, and plugin disclosure surfaces; source inspection shows adjacent primitives but no current contract to implement mechanically.

options.title: Sponsor a core policy design
options.body: Define a canonical provenance/action taxonomy and sensitive-target enforcement path before any implementation PR.

options.title: Expose plugin hook building blocks first
options.body: Narrow the work to hook/action metadata so external trusted-policy plugins can experiment without committing core enforcement yet.

options.title: Defer as hardening
options.body: Keep current exec approvals and trusted-operator model as the supported boundary and close or defer this direction until concrete user demand increases.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core policy design
recommendation.body: Define a canonical provenance/action taxonomy and sensitive-target enforcement path before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is in exec approval and node execution approval paths, which are central to sensitive-target enforcement.
